c0-frame.title: Frame the cycle
c0-frame.imperative: Refine-flavor grounding wave: chase cycle-1 open threads and test load-bearing assumptions via excursions BEFORE interface tightening. Owner chose to dispatch ALL 11 candidates (6 prior-art research R1-R6, 5 cheap prototypes P1-P5) in parallel: 'we never know what surprising things we might find.' Scoped-nulls discipline restated by owner: any null = state of that specific question, never a true null. Record pass when framed.
c0-frame.finding: Cycle 2 framed: refine-flavor grounding wave, all 11 excursions dispatched in parallel at owner's call

xR1.title: Research: lap-time simulation prior art (fidelity bounds)
xR1.imperative: One question: how do existing lap-time simulators (QSS vs transient, open-source and academic) formulate the ideal-lap problem and what fidelity suffices for relative comparisons? Bounds reference-lap fidelity needs.
xR1.finding: Field taxonomy 2x2 (QSS vs transient x fixed vs free trajectory); QSS+free-trajectory g-g-map hybrid = practical sweet spot; open-source tools all QSS. ESSENTIAL fidelity floor for RELATIVE comparison: load-sensitive tyre friction, combined-slip friction ellipse, speed-dependent aero - matches our capability-envelope stack. Quasi-static axle weight transfer needed to explain WHY (front/rear-limited). Mainly-absolute fidelity: full transient dynamics, tyre thermal, 3D track. Unresolved tension flagged: F1 teams frame relatively yet buy full fidelity; yaw-inertia shown to move lap time non-trivially. Validation numbers thin (OptimumLap vendor claim ~10% for bare point-mass). Full: excursions/R1-RESULT.md

xR2.title: Research: car-vs-driver decomposition literature
xR2.imperative: One question: what car/driver variance splits and methods has the F1 multilevel-modeling literature converged on? Bounds variance-decomposition expectations.
xR2.finding: Literature does NOT converge on car/driver split: constructor share 61-88% across sources; two most rigorous papers disagree by 24pts on same era (Bayesian ROL 88% vs RAPM ridge 64%), unresolved (DNF treatment/regularization suspected). CONVERGES on: teammate+switching identification; wet weather AND street circuits shift importance toward driver (the load-bearing external finding); ALL models additive with ZERO interaction terms; ALL fit ordinal outcomes (position/points) - NONE model lap time directly. No external prior art exists at corner-type/regime fingerprint granularity - we are past the literature. Full: excursions/R2-RESULT.md

xR3.title: Research: venue-fit priors in other sports (golf analog)
xR3.imperative: One question: how does golf course-fit modeling (skill-by-category x venue-composition) handle thin cells/shrinkage/replication, and how big do venue-fit effects turn out? Bounds join magnitude + estimation patterns.
xR3.finding: Golf = exact structural analog and a CAUTION: DataGolf course-fit adjustments tiny (+/-0.07 strokes/round typical, ~1 at tail mismatches); independent 119k-round walk-forward replication found residual shape-match has ZERO OOS predictive power after controlling overall skill (r=-0.019) - 'course fit is mostly just being good'. Transferable load-bearing patterns: category-dependent shrinkage (noisiest channel most shrunk), raw venue-history averaging = documented noise-mine trap, THE gate = held-out replication of the RESIDUAL fit effect after z-scoring out baseline skill. Baseball park factors = venue main effect (different animal), large at extremes, still 38% shrinkage. Honest prior: expect our driver-x-circuit interaction SMALL vs baseline driver skill until replication says otherwise. Full: excursions/R3-RESULT.md

xR4.title: Research: driver-style telemetry literature
xR4.imperative: One question: which telemetry observables has driver-identification/style research found discriminative? Bounds fingerprint observable choice.
xR4.finding: Brake + throttle PEDAL DYNAMICS (shape, not position) = most individually-identifying signals across the road-car driver-ID literature; braking-impulse features hit 88.9% for 30 drivers AT 10Hz (matches our rate). Trail-braking duration + steering smoothness top the sim-racing fast-vs-slow features. Key caveats: accuracy collapses with driver-pool size (none tested near 20); per-TURN discriminativeness varies wildly (33-93%) - 'driver corners' are real, corner SELECTION matters; identity-fingerprinting vs style-vs-pace are conflated questions in the literature. Confirmed ceiling: per-wheel/ABS-cycle detail needs 500-4000Hz, out of reach; coarse impulse/duration/slope features computable at 10-20Hz. GAP flagged: Loeckel DIMRA paper (pro race drivers, exactly our question) paywalled - the one follow-up worth institutional access. Full: excursions/R4-RESULT.md

xR5.title: Research: track evolution / grip modeling prior art
xR5.imperative: One question: how do engineering literature and analytics practice model intra- and inter-session grip evolution and FP-to-quali correction? Bounds grip-baseline design.
xR5.finding: No validated F1 track-evolution model exists anywhere public - the field is open. Best quantitative: hobbyist GAM (2021): evolution nonlinear in CUMULATIVE CAR-LAPS (not wall clock), ~0.75-1.0s/session at Abu Dhabi, big circuit spread. Practitioner form: saturating exponential in cumulative laps + zone-weighted deposition (braking 85% > cornering 55% > acceleration 25%). Inter-session: qualitative consensus only - dry sessions carry forward, rain = hard reset (unquantified), support series share the ledger unweighted. NULLS: no inter-session decay model, no FP->Q formula, no high-vs-low-load corner comparison, no peer-reviewed F1 paper. Full: excursions/R5-RESULT.md

xR6.title: Research: ERS deployment inference from speed traces
xR6.imperative: One question: what does the F1 energy-deployment optimal-control literature imply is inferable about deployment from speed/throttle traces alone? Bounds the energy channel.
xR6.finding: No peer-reviewed trace-to-ERS inversion exists; one 2026 arXiv preprint (HMM-POMDP framing) reports 92.3% for COARSE 3-level ERS state but synthetic-only. Real signatures are curved ramps vs drag baseline, NOT clean kinks (2026 MGU-K regulatory rampdown: 350kW below 290km/h tapering to 0 at 355km/h - explains P5's cliff-null). Honestly recoverable: relative deployment vs driver's own rolling baseline, phase structure (deploy straights/harvest braking), gross derate flags. NOT recoverable: exact SOC/kW, override state, deception. Unresolved source conflict: 8.5 vs 4.0 MJ per-lap harvest (likely different quantities). Design implication: energy channel = coarse relative + phase-level, with honest sigma. Full: excursions/R6-RESULT.md

xP1.title: Prototype: complete segment tiling spike (2-3 circuits)
xP1.imperative: One question: does a coherent complete tiling (corner classes + braking zones + straights, sector-nested) fall out of existing artifacts, and where do the three taxonomies disagree? THE load-bearing prerequisite.
xP1.finding: NO complete tiling falls out of existing artifacts. Only utilization 4-regime tiling (b) is complete; grip_bin_obs taxonomy (a) structurally incomplete (a_lat>3 gate = no opinion on straights); ephemeris (c) = 1 circuit, corner-vs-gap only. Disagreements are STRUCTURAL: (a) gates kinematic, (b) geometric -> trail-braking points classified differently; ephemeris corner windows start at turn-in not braking point; 10-16% of track distance flips label across drivers on (b). SURPRISE 4th taxonomy: src/physics/segment_classifier.py SegmentClassifier - complete by construction + already bridges to (a)'s MixtureFit via soft_class_membership, but standalone/not-wired, and disagrees with (b) 50x on curvature gate (0.005 vs 1e-4). FIA sector LOCATIONS not recoverable from any store (circuit_info empty; lap_times has durations only) - needs time-to-distance join against telemetry. Trap: tele_pos/tele_car SQLite empty, real data in Parquet via TelemetryStore only. Full: excursions/P1-RESULT.md

xP2.title: Prototype: utilization noise at class granularity
xP2.imperative: One question: what is per-class per-weekend sigma when #628 deficits are re-bucketed into the severity ladder — usable signal or noise at k=4? Bounds k empirically.
xP2.finding: USABLE SIGNAL at k=4, not mush: noise ratio (within-driver scatter / between-driver separation) flat going 2 macro corner regimes (2.32/2.39) -> 4 severity classes (1.93-2.40); each class ~309 pts/driver-weekend (BETTER supported than macro fast_corner ~163). Ran live #628 machinery read-only, 4 rounds x 3 constructors 2023 Q, zero errors. Key structure: much within-driver scatter is CLASS-INDEPENDENT weekend shift (Austria negative, Hungary positive) = inherited ceiling/circuit noise, exactly what a weekend-state term should absorb - finer binning adds no new noise. Caveats: n=4 weekends, quantile-bin proxy not real GMM, boundary circuit-stability untested. Full: excursions/P2-RESULT.md

xP3.title: Prototype: apex_obs fingerprint substrate smoke
xP3.imperative: One question: do per-driver radius-binned apex curves (2023) show split-half structure, raw and within-team-normalized? Cheap preview of replication on existing data.
xP3.finding: Thin, BIN-SPECIFIC signal survives cheap teammate control: 50-80m radius corners keep significant normalized split-half correlation in BOTH v_apex (r=0.459 p=0.036) and a_lat (r=0.594 p=0.004); a_lat also holds in 20-32m tight bin; 3/5 bins collapse to noise post-normalization; 80-126m trends negative (doesn't fit fingerprint story). Suggestive not confirmatory (no multiple-comparison correction; calendar-order split; no ceiling-norm/shrinkage). NOTE: apex_obs radius range is 8-200m not ~500m. Scoped to raw 2023-Q apex speeds under teammate-subtraction. Full: excursions/P3-RESULT.md

xP4.title: Prototype: sector-composition error check (Bahrain pilot)
xP4.imperative: One question: how big is today's boundary-placement error when ephemeris pilot segment times are composed against official sector times? Bounds composed-validation design.
xP4.finding: Premise correction (scoped): ephemeris corner_json is NOT a full-lap tiling - curvature-threshold corner arcs only, ~35% of lap by design (documented v1 limitation), straights deliberately excluded. So composed-sector validation is NOT buildable from current exports; needs full-lap tiling from the generator (P1's tiling is the fix). GOOD NEWS: official per-lap sector times DO exist on disk (data/f1_data_2023.db lap_times.sector1/2/3_time), and eph observed_lap_s matches official lap_time exactly on all 2471 rows (same ground truth). Coverage ratio is tight (stdev 1.6pp) = stable partial export, not boundary noise. Full: excursions/P4-RESULT.md

xP5.title: Prototype: per-segment energy accounting spike
xP5.imperative: One question: what does per-segment kinetic-energy bookkeeping from raw telemetry look like on one power-sensitive circuit, and what deployment signature is visible without ERS channels? Feasibility read on the energy channel.
xP5.finding: KE ledger WORKS mechanically: 7 straights auto-found per lap (consistent across 4 drivers, Monza 2023 Q), d(KE)/ds decays smoothly (power-limited-terminal-velocity textbook shape), per-segment net-power 68-390kW physically sane. SCOPED NULLS: no deployment cliff seen (negative about cliffs, NOT positive claim about strategy - 2023 deployment can't be separated from ICE without ERS channels); lap-to-lap pair showed nothing. DRS gives real modest dKE/ds uptick (3/4 drivers) needing matched-speed comparison to isolate. Ledger is net-work only; propulsion/drag split needs CdA model (which we HAVE in the estimate store - unplugged in this spike). Full: excursions/P5-RESULT.md

consolidation.summary: Cycle 2 grounding wave complete: 11/11 excursions returned, all verified fresh. Prior art bounds: interaction term expected small (golf analog: zero OOS residual power - demand residual-replication gate), driver importance IS circuit-conditional (wet/street external evidence), our sim already at essential fidelity floor, track evolution + trace-to-ERS = open fields (we build first from own data), brake/throttle dynamics = most identifying features AT our 10Hz rate, driver corners real (discriminativeness varies per corner). Prototypes: NO complete tiling exists (4 taxonomies, structural disagreements, 10-16% boundary instability, SegmentClassifier = unwired complete seed with mixture bridge); k=4 class granularity adds no noise (signal usable, weekend shifts dominate scatter); thin bin-specific apex fingerprint survives teammate control (50-80m); composed-sector validation needs full tiling (sector times ARE on disk); KE ledger works (deployment = coarse relative + phase only, 2026 rampdown explains cliff-null). Board updated; refined open threads seed next step.
